title: Kurogane Holly: Ancient Kurogane Hollies You Can Visit
meta_description: The register won't count a trunk under three metres. Three Kurogane hollies mapped, from a Kagoshima crossroads to a Hiroshima temple summit.
intro: Kurogane holly is a glossy-leaved evergreen of warm southern Japan that rarely gets large: Japan's giant-tree register will not count a trunk under three metres. Two of the three the site maps clear that easily. Kagoshima's Terukuni Park holly is thickest at 4.85 metres, multi-stemmed, standing at the crossroads where four national highways end; the city made it preserved tree number 6 in 1974, its first batch of designations. A second Kagoshima tree, in Gionnosu Park on land reclaimed from the Inari river mouth, has reached 2.4 metres since roughly the 1890s and now shares its ground with three nineteenth-century stone bridges moved there after a 1993 flood destroyed their originals. Higashi-Hiroshima's, on the temple mountain of Fukujo-ji, is the thinnest at 3.1 metres and the only one of the three with no recorded age.
